description: This is a group made of students willing and eager to learn more. This is an in-person group.
summary:
SPACEQUEST is an interactive browser-based space outpost simulation designed for children aged 7 to 12. Players take on the role of a Junior Flight Director commanding expeditions on the Moon (Shackleton Crater, Sea of Tranquility) and Mars (Jezero, Gale). Guided by Nova, a friendly
astronaut companion, young commanders balance limited resources—oxygen, power, radiation
shielding, and food—while executing six-step scientific missions. Every decision involves real
engineering trade-offs, where no choice is free. To ground learning in authentic space science,
SPACEQUEST integrates real NASA datasets, including DONKI solar flare records that trigger timed emergency alerts and OSDR biological studies. By turning complex aerospace constraints into accessible, visual gameplay without requiring downloads or accounts, SPACEQUEST empowers the next generation of explorers to understand how astronauts survive and conduct science beyond Earth.
details:
What It Does

SPACEQUEST places children aged 7 to 12 in command of a lunar or Martian outpost. Players enter their callsign, select their celestial body and landing site, and allocate a strict 10-point loadout budget across four vital systems: crew size (2 to 4 astronauts), power capacity (lightweight solar panels or high-density batteries), radiation shielding (standard or reinforced), and food supply (ready-to-eat rations or hydroponic dome). Players then execute six operational mission steps (rover travel, antenna deployment, core drilling, lab experiments, repairs, and Earth uplink) while responding to timed emergencies such as solar flares, dust storms, equipment failures, and communication latency.

How It Works & Technical Stack

The application is built as a static, browser-native web app (Next.js 15.5.29 static export, React 19.3.1, TypeScript 5.9.3) separating a pure, deterministic simulation engine from a diegetic command-console UI. A persistent procedural 3D scene (Three.js 0.170.0, React Three Fiber 9.8.2, Drei 10.7.9) renders the terrain, outpost hardware, and step cinematics, backed by a 2D parallax fallback (Stage2D) and procedural WebAudio sound effects. An interactive Data Lens lets players inspect whether every number comes from real NASA telemetry (REAL badge) or game balance rules (GAME RULE). Automated verification is powered by Vitest 3.2.7.

Benefits & Educational Goals

SPACEQUEST's core educational rule is that no action is free: a fast action drains power and increases breakdown risk, whereas a careful action preserves hardware at the cost of extra oxygen and food. Mission failures remain encouraging and constructive, explaining the physical cause of the loss while awarding "lesson learned" XP. The interface enforces youth accessibility standards (≥ 18 px typography, 48 px touch targets, full keyboard navigation, and a doubled-timer accessibility toggle).
